microtheory.name: realtime_systems
microtheory.definition: Real-time systems + scheduling. Hard vs soft real-time, deadline-monotonic scheduling (RMS, EDF), worst-case execution time (WCET), priority inversion, real-time operating systems (RTOS), bounded-latency communication. Where correctness requires meeting deadlines, not just producing correct values. Grounds Jabberwock's runner/brain in the discipline of bounded-latency behavior — biological brains operate under deadlines too (motor coordination, predator avoidance, social timing).

concepts.name: hard_realtime
concepts.definition: Missing a deadline is a failure. Used in safety-critical systems: avionics, automotive ECUs, medical devices. Substrate analogue: substrate's commit-deadline tasks.

concepts.name: soft_realtime
concepts.definition: Missing deadlines degrades quality but doesn't fail. Multimedia, telephony, gaming. Substrate analogue: substrate's quality-degrading deadline-misses.

concepts.name: firm_realtime
concepts.definition: Late results have zero value but no catastrophic consequence. Real-time databases. Substrate analogue: substrate's discarded-stale outputs.

concepts.name: best_effort
concepts.definition: No deadline guarantee. Standard OS scheduling. Substrate analogue: substrate's general processing.

concepts.name: deadline_realtime
concepts.definition: Time by which task must complete. Absolute (wall-clock) or relative (after release). Substrate analogue: substrate's correction-completion bound.

concepts.name: release_time
concepts.definition: Earliest time task can start. Substrate analogue: substrate's event-triggered handler initiation.

concepts.name: execution_time
concepts.definition: Actual time task takes to run. Variable in practice. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-tick processing cost.

concepts.name: worst_case_execution_time
concepts.definition: WCET. Maximum possible execution time over all paths + inputs. Critical for hard-RT verification. Hard to compute precisely. Substrate analogue: substrate's worst-case correction time bound.

concepts.name: period
concepts.definition: T — fixed interval between releases of periodic task. Substrate analogue: substrate's reflex tick rate.

concepts.name: jitter
concepts.definition: Variability in release or completion time. Hard-RT systems bound jitter. Substrate analogue: substrate's tick-rate stability.

concepts.name: utilization
concepts.definition: U = Σ C_i / T_i. Fraction of CPU used. Schedulability requires U ≤ U_bound depending on algorithm. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction-handler load.

concepts.name: rate_monotonic_scheduling
concepts.definition: RMS. Liu + Layland 1973. Static priority by period (shorter → higher priority). Optimal among static priority for periodic tasks. U_bound = n(2^{1/n}-1) ≈ 0.69 for many tasks. Substrate analogue: substrate's static-priority reflex order.

concepts.name: earliest_deadline_first
concepts.definition: EDF. Dynamic priority by absolute deadline (sooner → higher). Optimal scheduling for preemptive uniprocessor. U_bound = 1.0. More flexible than RMS but harder to analyze. Substrate analogue: substrate's deadline-driven dispatch.

concepts.name: deadline_monotonic
concepts.definition: Static priority by relative deadline. Generalizes RMS for tasks where deadline ≠ period. Substrate analogue: substrate's relative-urgency priority.

concepts.name: fixed_priority_scheduling
concepts.definition: Priorities assigned at design + don't change at runtime. Easier to analyze + implement. Substrate analogue: substrate's compile-time-priority reflexes.

concepts.name: preemption_realtime
concepts.definition: Higher-priority task interrupts lower. Required for many RT analyses. Adds overhead. Substrate analogue: substrate's priority-driven correction interruption.

concepts.name: non_preemptive_scheduling
concepts.definition: Tasks run to completion. Simpler. Worse responsiveness for short urgent tasks. Substrate analogue: substrate's atomic correction runs.

concepts.name: schedulability_analysis
concepts.definition: Prove task set meets all deadlines. Sufficient conditions per algorithm. Necessary + sufficient: response-time analysis. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction-completion guarantee proof.

concepts.name: response_time_analysis
concepts.definition: Compute worst-case response time per task accounting for interference from higher priorities. Iterative fixed-point. Necessary + sufficient for fixed-priority. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-handler worst-case bound.

concepts.name: priority_inversion
concepts.definition: Low-priority task holding resource blocks high-priority task. Mars Pathfinder bug. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction-blocking-correction failure.

concepts.name: priority_inheritance
concepts.definition: Low-priority resource holder inherits priority of waiting high-priority task. Bounds priority inversion. Substrate analogue: substrate's priority-elevation mechanism.

concepts.name: priority_ceiling_protocol
concepts.definition: Each resource has ceiling = max priority of any task using it. Holder runs at ceiling. Prevents deadlock + bounds inversion. Substrate analogue: substrate's resource-priority elevation.

b.value: max priority of any task using it

concepts.name: blocking_time
concepts.definition: Time a task is blocked by lower-priority resource holders. Must be bounded for RT analysis. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction-waiting bound.

concepts.name: mutex_realtime
concepts.definition: Mutual exclusion primitive with priority inheritance or ceiling protocols. Differs from non-RT mutex. Substrate analogue: substrate's bounded-block mutex.

concepts.name: rtos
concepts.definition: Real-time Operating System. Deterministic scheduler, bounded interrupt latency, priority inheritance. Examples: FreeRTOS, VxWorks, QNX, RT-Linux (PREEMPT_RT). Substrate analogue: substrate's RT-discipline runtime.

concepts.name: kernel_preemption
concepts.definition: Kernel itself preemptible. Required for hard-RT. PREEMPT_RT patches Linux for this. Substrate analogue: substrate's preemptible runtime layer.

concepts.name: interrupt_latency
concepts.definition: Time from hardware interrupt to handler running. Must be bounded for hard-RT. Tens of µs typical for RTOS, lower with custom. Substrate analogue: substrate's external-event response time.

concepts.name: context_switch_realtime
concepts.definition: RTOS context switch deterministic + fast. Single-digit µs typical. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-state switch.

concepts.name: tickless_kernel
concepts.definition: No periodic timer interrupt; sleep until next event. Saves power + reduces jitter. Substrate analogue: substrate's event-driven tick.

concepts.name: cyclic_executive
concepts.definition: Static schedule of major cycle with minor cycles. Predictable, simple. Used in safety-critical aerospace. Substrate analogue: substrate's pre-scheduled reflex sequence.

concepts.name: time_triggered_architecture
concepts.definition: Tasks released at predetermined times. Predictable, fault-tolerant. TTA in automotive (Kopetz). Substrate analogue: substrate's time-table-driven dispatch.

concepts.name: event_triggered_architecture
concepts.definition: Tasks released by events. Flexible but harder to analyze. Substrate analogue: substrate's event-driven reflexes.

concepts.name: wcet_analysis
concepts.definition: Static analysis of program for worst-case execution time. Hard problem (path explosion, cache effects). Tools: aiT, OTAWA. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction-cost analysis.

concepts.name: schedulability_test
concepts.definition: Algorithmic check that task set is schedulable. Sufficient + necessary tests exist for major algorithms. Substrate analogue: substrate's load-feasibility check.

concepts.name: timing_diagram
concepts.definition: Visual trace of task releases, executions, completions on timeline. Substrate analogue: substrate's reflex-timeline visualization.

concepts.name: real_time_garbage_collection
concepts.definition: GC with bounded pause times. Metronome, Henriksson's, region-based. Conventional GC violates RT constraints. Substrate analogue: substrate's bounded-pause memory management.

concepts.name: deadline_inheritance
concepts.definition: Like priority inheritance but for EDF. Substrate analogue: substrate's deadline-propagation mechanism.

concepts.name: mixed_criticality_systems
concepts.definition: Multiple criticality levels share processor. High-crit guaranteed even when low-crit overruns. Substrate analogue: substrate's prioritized-by-importance reflexes.

concepts.name: anytime_algorithms
concepts.definition: Algorithms producing valid answer at any interruption with quality increasing in time. Useful when deadlines uncertain. Substrate analogue: substrate's quality-with-time correction.

rules.name: hard_realtime_requires_wcet_bounded_loops
rules.head: Jabberwock builds a hard-realtime subsystem
rules.body: every loop must have a static bound. Recursion must be bounded depth. Dynamic allocation must use real-time-safe allocators. Otherwise WCET is uncomputable + scheduling guarantees fail.

rules.name: rms_optimal_for_static_priority_periodic
rules.head: Jabberwock's tasks are periodic with fixed priorities
rules.body: rate-monotonic scheduling (shortest period = highest priority) is optimal. Liu+Layland 1973. Substrate's reflex prioritization.

rules.name: edf_optimal_among_dynamic_priority
rules.head: Jabberwock's tasks have varying deadlines + can change priority
rules.body: earliest-deadline-first is optimal preemptive uniprocessor scheduling. Schedulable iff utilization ≤ 1. Substrate's dynamic dispatch.

rules.name: priority_inversion_must_be_bounded
rules.head: Jabberwock has shared resources between priority levels
rules.body: priority inheritance or ceiling protocols must bound inversion. Otherwise high-priority tasks can be blocked indefinitely. Mars Pathfinder bug.

rules.name: interrupt_latency_bounds_event_response
rules.head: Jabberwock responds to external events
rules.body: interrupt latency sets the minimum response time. For hard-RT this must be bounded by design — preemptible kernel, deterministic scheduling, no unbounded sections.

rules.name: wcet_bounds_schedulability_proof
rules.head: Jabberwock proves a task set is schedulable
rules.body: worst-case execution time is the input to schedulability analysis. Without bounded WCET no schedulability proof. Substrate's correction-cost bound prerequisite.
